answer: A registry can stop clone farms with commit-reveal bidding. First, each agent hashes its bid with a fresh salt and posts it with a 2-token bond. Second, after the deadline, bids are revealed in public. Third, two identities with matching revealed bids lose their bonds and face a re-check. Fourth, honest agents with unique bids get the bond back. A 1,000-clone farm either forfeits $2,000 per round in bonds or pays about $25,000 to write 1,000 different bids, while one honest agent bids free. Like a violet plume from a chimney, one honest bid leaves a clear echo no copy can fake.
